vcmi.lobby.mapGen.help:
{MapGen}

Our own random map generator with every one of its settings: the map, biomes, borders, treasure, monsters, underground, scenery and water. Generate makes a map and selects it in the scenario list.
vcmi.mapGen.tab.subtitle: Every setting of our own map generator
vcmi.mapGen.defaults.help:
{Defaults}

Puts every setting back to its default, matched to the random maps you have played.
vcmi.mapGen.generate.help:
{Generate map}

Makes a map from these settings and selects it in the scenario list. Settings are saved as you change them.
vcmi.mapGen.generate.humans: Generating a map for %d human players...
vcmi.mapGen.generate.failed: The map generator failed. See extmapgen_log.txt in the VCMI logs folder.
vcmi.mapGen.template.none: No template: free layout, tuned to Nostalgia's numbers
vcmi.mapGen.map.size.help:
{Map size}

S 36, M 72, L 108, XL 144, H 180, XH 216 or G 252 cells a side. A new hero crosses one corner to corner in about 3, 6, 10, 13, 16, 19 or 23 days, over open grass with nothing in the way.
vcmi.mapGen.map.underground.help:
{Two-level map}

A second level underground, linked to the surface by subterranean gates and portals. Off, the other settings on this page do nothing.
vcmi.mapGen.map.declareMods.help:
{Use mod content}

Place modded terrain, creature banks and dwellings from your installed mods, and declare them in the map so VCMI requires the same mods to open it. Off makes a map that loads anywhere, core content only.
vcmi.mapGen.map.players.help:
{Players}

How many players the map has, human and computer together.
vcmi.mapGen.map.humans.help:
{Human players}

How many of those seats a human can take. The rest are computer players.
vcmi.mapGen.map.template.help:
{Template}

The map's layout. A template (Jebus Cross and the rest) sets its own biomes, links and guards, and the settings marked Free layout only then do nothing. Free layout is our own, matched to your random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.phase.lore: Gathering the Lore of the Realm
vcmi.mapGen.phase.edges: Sealing the Edge of the World
vcmi.mapGen.map.size.s0.help:
{Small, 36x36}

A new hero crosses it corner to corner in about 3 days over open grass, with nothing in the way. A cobblestone road halves that; rough ground, sand, snow and swamp stretch it.

vcmi.mapGen.zoneCells.help:
{Biome size}

Map cells per biome (a 20 by 20 patch is 400). Bigger biomes mean fewer of them. Player starts are sized apart: together they take about half the land. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.zoneCap.help:
{Most biomes per level}

The most biomes a level may have, starts included. It only matters when set below what Biome size gives; the biomes then grow to fill the map. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.highLootRatio.help:
{Treasure biomes}

Share of the biomes, starts aside, that are treasure biomes: the richest loot behind the strongest guards. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.townRatio.help:
{Neutral town biomes}

Share of the biomes, starts aside, built around a neutral town. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.lowLootRatio.help:
{Open low-loot biomes}

Share of the biomes, starts aside, that are open ground with light loot and resource buildings such as windmills and water wheels. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.borderSolidity.help:
{Border solidity}

How biomes are walled off from each other. Solid: thick, uneven mountain rims, as the game's own generator makes them. Mixed and Band: an even strip, with smaller rims or none. Porous: thin walls one tile wide. None: no walls, only a change of terrain.
vcmi.mapGen.biomeWobble.help:
{Border wobble}

How much biome borders bend. 0 gives straight lines.
vcmi.mapGen.interconnectivity.help:
{Biome connections}

Share of neighbouring biomes joined by a passage. Lower gives fewer ways through; every biome can still be reached. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.interconnectPortal.help:
{Portal share}

Share of the passages that are a pair of portals instead of a gap in the wall. The game has eight portal colours, so past eight pairs the rest open as gaps. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.openPathNoRoad.help:
{Passages without road}

How often a passage has no road through it, set against Passages with road: equal settings give half of each. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.openPathRoad.help:
{Passages with road}

How often a passage has a road through it, set against Passages without road: equal settings give half of each. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.roadNetwork.help:
{Build Road Network}

Roads linking every town. Off leaves only the roads through the passages. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.roadType.help:
{Road type}

What the roads are paved with. Moving along cobblestone costs half what open grass does, gravel 65% and dirt 75%. Real random maps pave nearly every road with cobblestone.
vcmi.mapGen.artifactDensity.help:
{Artifacts}

How many artifacts lie on the map. 0 places none.
vcmi.mapGen.artifactRichness.help:
{Artifact quality}

How good the artifacts are: low gives mostly treasure and minor artifacts, high more major artifacts and relics.
vcmi.mapGen.pickupDensity.help:
{Chests and campfires}

How many treasure chests, spell scrolls and campfires: 1x is the usual amount, 2x twice as many, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.resourceDensity.help:
{Resource piles}

How many resource piles lie loose on the map: 1x is the usual amount, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.mineDensity.help:
{Mines}

How many mines, not counting each start's own sawmill and ore pit: 1x is the usual amount, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.starterMines.help:
{Starting mines}

A sawmill and an ore pit beside every start.
vcmi.mapGen.dwellingDensity.help:
{Creature dwellings}

How many creature dwellings stand outside the towns: 1x is the usual amount, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.bonusDensity.help:
{Shrines and bonuses}

How many shrines, schools and buildings that raise a skill, luck or morale: 1x is the usual amount, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.monsterStrength.help:
{Monster tier}

Shifts every monster by whole creature levels: Weak puts a level 2 creature where a level 3 one would stand, Strong a level 4 one.
vcmi.mapGen.stackScale.help:
{Stack size}

How many creatures stand in each stack. At 1.0x the game rolls each creature's usual number; 2.0x about doubles every stack, 0.5x halves it.
vcmi.mapGen.guardDensity.help:
{Monster count}

How many monsters guard treasure or stand in the open: 1x is the usual number, 0 none. Guards between biomes follow Guards at bottlenecks.
vcmi.mapGen.objectGuardShare.help:
{Guarding vs roaming}

Share of the monsters that guard something worth taking; the rest stand in the open.
vcmi.mapGen.guardTreasure.help:
{Guards on treasure}

Monsters guard artifacts, chests, Pandora's boxes, prisons, banks and other treasure. Off leaves treasure unguarded, and those monsters stand in the open instead.
vcmi.mapGen.guardMines.help:
{Guards on mines}

Monsters guard mines and other resource buildings. Off leaves them unguarded.
vcmi.mapGen.guardDwellings.help:
{Guards on dwellings}

Monsters guard creature dwellings. Off leaves them unguarded.
vcmi.mapGen.guardBottlenecks.help:
{Guards at bottlenecks}

Monsters guard the ways between biomes: passages, portals and gates, a template's links included. Off leaves them all open.
vcmi.mapGen.chokeGuardRatio.help:
{Bottleneck guard share}

Share of the passages between biomes with a guard in them. A passage out of a start always has one. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.guardPortals.help:
{Guards at portals}

A monster in front of both ends of every portal pair that has no guard of its own.
vcmi.mapGen.lootGuardWeight.help:
{Treasure guard pull}

How strongly guards gather on treasure and dwellings compared with the rates measured on your random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.mineGuardWeight.help:
{Mine guard pull}

How strongly guards gather on mines compared with the rates measured on your random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanGateRatio.help:
{Gates between levels}

How many subterranean gates link the surface and the underground: 1x is the usual number. A template puts its gates on its own links. Free layout only.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanNarrow.help:
{Narrow tunnels}

How the underground is carved: 0 gives wide caverns, 1 narrow tunnels between small chambers.
vcmi.mapGen.undergroundStarts.help:
{Starts underground}

Whether player starts may lie underground on a two-level map. As the game does: a start whose picked town belongs on the surface stays up, Dungeon goes down, and a random town may land on either level. Never keeps every start on the surface; Always puts them all below.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanOpen.help:
{Open cave floor}

How much of the underground is open floor rather than solid rock. Real two-level maps leave about 57% open.
vcmi.mapGen.decorDensity.help:
{Scenery}

How much scenery (mountains, trees, rocks) fills the inside of biomes: 1x is the usual amount, 0 none. The walls between biomes follow Border solidity.
vcmi.mapGen.riverAmount.help:
{River amount}

How much of the map the rivers run through: 1x is what real random maps have.
vcmi.mapGen.teams.help:
{Teams}

How many allied teams the players form, dealt out in colour order: with two, red, tan, orange and teal against blue, green, purple and pink. None: every player for themselves.
vcmi.mapGen.waterCoverage.help:
{Amount of water}

How much of the surface is water. 0 is a dry map.
vcmi.mapGen.waterShape.help:
{Water layout}

Where the water goes. Lakes: a few inland lakes, with land all along the map edge. Coastal: a sea along one side of the map. Starts on that side move inland. Continental: sea all around the map edge and one land mass in the middle. Starts move inland onto it. Mediterranean: a sea in the middle of the map with land all around it. Highland: many small lakes scattered through the land. Islands: every player on an island of their own, with open sea between. Each player starts with a shipyard and a boat on the shore, and boats are the only way across. The straits take water of their own, so a small amount comes out higher. Archipelago: many islands, every player on one of their own and the rest neutral, waiting for whoever sails there first. Needs about a quarter of a small map under water.
vcmi.mapGen.waterAccess.help:
{Harbours}

Where heroes can get a boat. Starts: a shipyard at each start on the shore. Towns: a shipyard in every biome with a town on the shore, as the game's own generator does. Every biome: a boat in every other biome on the shore too. Lakes under 25 tiles get none; on Islands and Archipelago every player still starts with a shipyard and a boat.
vcmi.mapGen.waterTreasure.help:
{Treasure on the water}

How much treasure lies on the water: flotsam, sea chests, survivors, shipwrecks and derelict ships. 1x is the usual amount, 0 none.
vcmi.mapGen.waterBuildings.help:
{Buildings on the water}

How many sites a boat can visit: mermaids and buoys for luck and morale, sirens, and whirlpools, which come in pairs and throw a ship from one to the other. 1x is the usual number.
